_readme: Hand-labelled numeric claims across the four event bundles. This is the
answer key for the Stage 9 contradiction-detection F1 and the Stage 14
It has TWO halves, and both are load-bearing:
contradictions - figures that genuinely disagree and MUST be surfaced.
agreements     - figures reported by several sources that AGREE and must
NOT be flagged. Without these there are no true
negatives, so precision is undefined and an agent that
flags everything would score a perfect recall and look
excellent. They are the reason this file is not just a
Every value here was checked against the cited source. Where the project
brief asserted a figure we could not confirm, it is marked unverified
rather than promoted to ground truth.
tolerance_note: Two figures count as the same claim if within reporter.numeric_reconciliation.relative_tolerance (2%) of each other. Rounding differences are not contradictions.

contradictions.description: Peer-reviewed sources differ by a factor of ~3 on how many people died. Neither is obviously wrong: they may count different things (confirmed deaths vs. deaths plus presumed-dead missing) over different reporting windows. The correct behaviour is to report the range and the disagreement, never to average or pick.

values.qualifier: at least; reported 3 days after the event during an active search

contradictions.expected_reporting: Sources report between 40 and 178 fatalities; Sattar et al. (Science, 2025) give 55 dead and 74 missing, while Zhang et al. (Landslides, 2024) give 178 fatalities.

contradictions.description: A 14% difference in the collapsed moraine volume between the two peer-reviewed reconstructions. Above the 2% tolerance, so a genuine disagreement, but far less severe than the fatality spread.

The flagship demonstration. One source states outright that the count varies from 4 to 11 across reporting. An agent that silently picks one number here is exactly the failure mode this project argues against.

values.qualifier: totalling 405 MW plus a 25 MW solar project
count of HEPs whose generation was halted, ~250 MW - a different quantity being conflated in reporting
explicit statement that the figure varies from 4, 5, 8 to 11

contradictions.expected_reporting: Sources report between 4 and 11 damaged hydropower projects; the spread partly reflects different definitions (damaged vs. generation halted vs. under construction).

contradictions.description: Death and missing counts differ roughly two-fold across the government report and independent analysis.

A single document contradicts ITSELF: it states 23 human casualties, then itemises 19 deaths, 13 missing and 1 injured, which sum to 33. An agent that only compares figures across documents will miss this entirely. It is included to make sure intra-document consistency is actually being checked.

Three sources give three incompatible before/after pairs for the same two days. The pre-event figures span 0.638 to 0.75 km2 (18% spread) and the post-event figures span 0.435 to 0.60 km2 (38% spread). Directly relevant to the watcher, since these are the areas our own delineation must be compared against.

Not a numeric contradiction but a categorical one, and the single most important thing to get right in this bundle. Early media described Chamoli as a glacier burst or GLOF; the peer-reviewed analysis identifies a rock-and-ice avalanche with no lake involved. The reporter must side with the primary source AND surface that the early characterisation was wrong.
contradictions.required_output_behaviour: Must NOT label Chamoli a GLOF in the structured hazard record or in the sitrep text, in either language.

contradictions.description: ICIMOD's own page dates the Thame study 14 Oct 2025; the project brief says 15 Oct 2025. A one-day discrepancy in a publication date is noise, not a finding. Included as a deliberate LOW-severity case: an agent that escalates this to the sitrep is over-flagging, and severity calibration is part of what Stage 14 measures.

values.note: not in any bundle document; recorded for completeness

agreements.description: Total released volume. Internally consistent: 156,000 from the upper lake plus 303,000 from the lower sums exactly to the stated total. Must NOT be flagged.
Reported consistently. Must NOT be flagged.
The pre-event area, consistent with the stated 2017-2023 stable range of 32,881-41,758 m2. Central to the project's argument and must survive into the sitrep unflagged.
The post-burst area drop, reported once with stated uncertainty. No competing figure exists. Must NOT be flagged.

Teesta III capacity, uncontested across sources. Must NOT be flagged - and note it coexists with the disputed project COUNT in the Rasuwa bundle, so an agent cannot simply treat all hydropower figures as suspect.

The Rasuwagadhi plant capacity is 111 MW in both the NEA statement and the SANDRP itemisation. Agreement inside an otherwise heavily contested bundle: the agent must not flag it just because neighbouring figures disagree.
Uncontested in the bundle. Must NOT be flagged.

Reported as an open-ended 'more than 200'. An open bound is not a contradiction with a specific figure unless one falls below it. Tests that the agent handles qualifiers rather than treating every inequality as a disagreement.
